title: feat(lint): export the dataset dimension leg group-key classifier groupKeyClassOf
body:
Fixes #23235

Clause-②: yes

## What

`@objectstack/lint` now exports the dataset dimension leg's group-key classifier from the package barrel:

- **`groupKeyClassOf(shape: ValueShapeFieldDef): GroupKeyClass | null`**. `null` means the column stores one scalar value and the analytics door serves it as a group key. Otherwise it names the JSON-stored class the door refuses with `400 INVALID_FIELD`: `'structured-json'` (`STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES`) or `'multi-value'` (`isMultiValueField`). The two spec predicates are applied in the door's order.
- **`GroupKeyClass`** = `'structured-json' | 'multi-value'`, the named result type. `jsonStoredDimensionFinding` now uses it in place of the inline literal union.

`dimension-json-stored-field-refused` keeps calling the same function on both legs (dataset dimensions at the `datasets[i].dimensions[k].field` site, cube dimensions at the `analyticsCubes[i].dimensions.NAME.sql` site). The barrel re-exports the function the module defines. There is no wrapper and no second copy. The rule's findings, paths and texts are unchanged: no existing assertion in the rule's suite was edited.

## Why this input shape, and no wrapper

The brief asked whether a consumer must pass `ValueShapeFieldDef` or whether a wrapper should take a field definition. Measured on `main`:

- `ValueShapeFieldDef` is not private. `@objectstack/spec/data` exports it (`field-value.zod.ts`). It is the value contract's structural slice of a field definition: `type`, `multiple`, `options`. Its docblock says it is structural so callers holding their own field-def types can pass theirs as they are.
- The consumer holds a field definition. A spec `Field` is assignable to it, so `groupKeyClassOf(field)` works with no adapter. A new case pins this at compile time: three `Field` literals (`tags`, `select` with `multiple: true`, a plain `select`) are passed with no cast. The lint package's test layer is type-checked, and `check:test-typecheck` is OK for `packages/lint/tsconfig.test.json`.
- The analytics door's own classifier (`groupedClassOf` in `service-analytics/src/structured-json-dimension-door.ts`) takes the same `ValueShapeFieldDef`. The export accepts exactly the shape the door judges, so the input is not widened. A wrapper over a field definition would add a second signature for the same verdict.
- The classifier reads no object graph. Resolving a dotted path to its leaf is still the caller's job, and the JSDoc and the changeset say so.

## Pin: the export and the rule agree on the rule's own fixtures

New describe block `[#23235] groupKeyClassOf — the exported classifier and the rule agree on the rule's own fixtures`. It imports the classifier through `./index.js`, the consumer's door:

1. The barrel export is the module's function (`toBe` identity).
2. **Dataset leg sweep.** For every `FieldType.options` entry, with and without `multiple: true`, the export's answer equals the class named in the rule's finding, or `null` when the rule is silent, on the rule's own `dimensionStack` fixture. Floors are exact on the two refusing classes (`2 × STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES.size` and `2 × MULTI_OPTION_TYPES.size + MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES.size`) and more than 50 on the served side, so a classifier that always answers the same thing cannot make the agreement vacuous.
3. **Named fixtures.** The dimension leg's own shapes (`json`, `text`, `multiselect`, `checkboxes`, `tags`, `select` with `multiple: true`, `select`) give the same expected class from both the export and the rule.
4. **Cube leg.** Every typed column of the cube leg's own `cubeStack` fixture object (`fx_ledger`) gives the same answer as the rule's cube dimension finding. All three answers are exercised.
5. **A declared `Field` passes verbatim** (see above).

The class is read from the finding's message words (`a structured-JSON value` / `a multi-value field`) and the column name. Several findings, or words naming no class or both, read as `'unreadable'`, which no classifier answer equals.

### Ablation (each leg's call site replaced by a type-only private copy)

Both runs went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` under the verify lock. The anchor hit once and moved 1 -> 0. Each run restored: the blob after restore equals the HEAD blob `3fc39652c3ac` and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The test file imports `src` through relative paths, so no `dist` is involved.

- Dataset leg (`const cls = groupKeyClassOf(shape);` replaced by a `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES`-only check): **4 failed / 61 passed (65)**. Two of the failures are the new pins: `agrees with the dataset leg on every declared FieldType…` and `agrees with the dimension leg on its named fixtures`.
- Cube leg (`const cls = groupKeyClassOf(column.shape);` replaced the same way): **3 failed / 62 passed (65)**. One of the failures is the new pin: `agrees with the cube leg on every column of the cube fixture`.

The observed direction is red, as expected.

## Landing spot

As claimed: `packages/lint/src/validate-dataset-measure-aggregates.ts`, `packages/lint/src/index.ts`, the rule's test file, and `.changeset/23235-export-group-key-classifier.md` (`@objectstack/lint: minor`, `Clause-②: yes`, additive). `@objectstack/lint` has no API-surface snapshot. `check:published-readme-exports` is green, and the lint README lists no exports.

## Verification (final head `dfe60e348`)

- `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/lint^...' build`: exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint build`: exit 0, `check-dts-emitted` 6/6. `groupKeyClassOf` and `GroupKeyClass` are in `dist/index.d.ts`, and the CJS (`dist/index.cjs`) and ESM entries both load and answer `multi-value` / `structured-json` / `null`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: **139 files / 6731 tests passed**.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` + `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run test:repo`: **60 files / 1029 tests passed** (spec rebuilt after merging `origin/main`).
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 62 commands, plus `check:published-readme-exports`, `check-changeset-fixed.mjs` and `check:error-code-casing` from the roster block. All exit 0 except:
  - `check:where-matcher` failed on the first draft of the pin's helper. Its structural discovery seated the helper as a WHERE matcher (`Object.keys(...)` over a same-file map plus an indexed first parameter). The helper was rewritten to destructure and to read a `Map`. The gate is now green: 0 new matchers, baseline unchanged.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure` printed **PREREQUISITE NOT MET** (exit 3): they need a whole-workspace `dist/`. These are NOT MEASURED locally and are declared to CI. The lint package's own CJS/ESM load was probed directly (above).

## Acceptance notes

- **The door keeps its own copy.** `service-analytics`' `structured-json-dimension-door.ts` composes the same two predicates in a private `groupedClassOf`. That is a second account of the door's order, inside the door itself. The two agree today: same predicates, same order, same input type. They are held equal only by each side's sweep against `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES` / `isMultiValueField`, not by a shared call. `service-analytics` does not depend on `@objectstack/lint` (that direction is wrong), so one copy for both would have to live in `@objectstack/spec/data`. That is a different card's decision. Carrier: none.
- Cloud's switch from `dataset-derive.ts` `isDimensionField` to this export is cloud's card, per the triage direction.
